message.content:
**Answer:** One of the most celebrated and widely recognized sculptures of the 19th century is **“The Kiss” (Le Baiser) by Auguste Rodin**, finished in 1889. **Why it’s considered so famous** | Feature | Details | |---------|---------| | **Artist** | Auguste Rodin – often called the “father of modern sculpture.” | | **Date** | 1889 (first version; subsequent casts made later). | | **Style** | Realist/Impressionist blend; captures intimate human emotion with naturalistic detail. | | **Impact** | • Became an icon of romantic love and artistic freedom.
• Influenced countless artists and became a staple in museums worldwide.
• Its dramatic pose and expressive faces set a new standard for figurative sculpture. | | **Legacy** | • Frequently reproduced in various media (bronze, marble, plaster).
• Continues to be referenced in popular culture, literature, and film. | While other monumental works—such as **the Statue of Liberty** (completed 1886), **Rodin’s “The Gates of Hell”** (begun 1880), and **Gustave Moreau’s “The Love of the Hesperides”** (1875)—were also highly influential, “The Kiss” stands out for its universal appeal and enduring presence in both art history and everyday life. --- **Short answer:** *Auguste Rodin’s “The Kiss” (1889) is arguably the most famous sculpture of the 19th century.*
